overall_assessment: The multi-reviewer assignment, conflict adjudication, and collaboration boundaries implemented in searchright-screening and searchright-governance strictly conform to sound methodological research standards (PRISMA-S / PRISMA-LSR contracts) and institutional collaboration requirements. The ScreeningBoard enforces reviewer role segregation (ReviewerRole::Screener, ReviewerRole::Adjudicator, ReviewerRole::PolicyAdmin) and strict adjudication independence: any primary reviewer who has already submitted a screening decision for a subject is barred from adjudicating a conflict on that subject (failing closed with ScreeningError::AdjudicatorNotIndependent). The non-negotiable human-in-the-loop mandate is structurally encoded in ScreeningBoard::confirm_agent_exclusion: autonomous agents are incapable of self-executing study exclusions without explicit, auditable human confirmation. Blinded views (BlindedDecisionView) prevent bias during dual-independent screening rounds by masking peer decisions, rationales, and exclusion reasons until official conflict resolution is initiated. The federated artefact threat model in docs/security/threat-model.md documents boundary protections, replay risks, and pilot prerequisites, while keeping claims bounded to source-verified implementation without unwarranted promotion.
verified_invariants: adjudicator independence: screeners cannot adjudicate conflicting decisions on records they previously screened (ScreeningError::AdjudicatorNotIndependent)
mandatory human confirmation of agent exclusions: autonomous agents cannot exclude studies without explicit human confirmation in confirm_agent_exclusion
blinded screening segregation: BlindedDecisionView masks peer decisions, rationales, and exclusion reasons during active dual screening
governed amendments and re-screening: post-decision modifications require structured ScreeningAmendment and ReScreenRequest with auditable justifications
role-gated screening board operations: assign_role, revoke_role, and resolve require validated reviewer authorizations
federated collaboration threat boundaries: threat-model.md explicitly enumerates participant compromise, poisoned exchange packets, and data leak vectors

findings.description: Multi-reviewer conflict resolution and independent adjudication are verified across unit tests and board_edges.rs integration tests; multi-institution cross-site collaborative screening pilots remain an open gate.
findings.recommendation: Maintain open gate T28-G-CROSS-INSTITUTION-PILOT until inter-institutional trials are executed.

findings.description: The system preserves separate identifiers for records, studies, and reports, ensuring federated exchange packets do not conflate bibliographic records with methodological screening authority.
findings.recommendation: Preserve explicit linkage and provenance across all future multi-tenant or federated adapters.

assertions_evaluated.notes: Multi-reviewer assignment, conflict resolution, and independent human adjudication are enforced in source and verified in Rust and Python test suites.
Federated artefact threat model is documented in docs/security/threat-model.md; prerequisites are explicit and open gates are honestly preserved.

limitations: Source-verified implementation only; live multi-reviewer enterprise pilots and cross-institutional artefact exchange trials remain gated.
